```{r setup, message=FALSE}
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(stringr)
library(tibble)
library(readr)
library(googledrive)
library(arrow)
library(ggplot2)
theme_set(theme_bw())

RAW_DIR <- "Raw_Data/"

# This is the root folder with all dates
# (but if local drive space is an issue, you can also use a
# date-specific folder on google drive)
GDRIVE_FOLDER <- "https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1ETfZoritHHmPS0X4vXFLmjBlqMCS8OK8"
# For example, this is the 20260604 folder
# GDRIVE_8100_FOLDER <- "https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/107du2DkwDA2VpeqxdegbSe_dCoVvgpmP"

PROCESSED_FILE <- file.path("Processed_Data",
                            "SoilFluxes_8100_Metadata_processed.parquet")
PROCESSED_FILE_FINAL <- gsub("processed.parquet", 
                             "processed_final.parquet",
                             PROCESSED_FILE)
```

## What this code does

1. Download ALL the LI-8100 and 7810 data files from the Google Drive. Existing files will be skipped.
2. Separate 8100 file into each flux. This generates a huge (almost 200K) number of files, but they're small.
3. Extract metadata from each flux file into a metadata sheet. This is slow but we save progress as we go, so data updates don't require re-reading everything.
4. The final metadata is saved as `r PROCESSED_FILE_FINAL`.

**Need to figure out how to incorporate the 8100 error log 
(remove those fluxes?)**

## Download zipped 81x files into raw data folder

```{r download-8100}
options(googledrive_quiet = TRUE)

# Filter to necessary files
files_pulse <- drive_ls(path = GDRIVE_FOLDER,
                        recursive = TRUE,
                        pattern = "81x$")

message("Found ", nrow(files_pulse), " files")

download_files <- function(files_pulse) {
    # Download files to local directory
    invisible(
        lapply(seq_len(nrow(files_pulse)), function(i) {
            outfile <- file.path(RAW_DIR, files_pulse$name[i])
            message(i, " ", basename(outfile))
            if(file.exists(outfile)) {
                message("\tskipped existing file ")
            } else {
                message("\tdownloading...")
                drive_download(
                    file = as_id(files_pulse$id[i]),
                    path = outfile,
                    overwrite = TRUE
                )
            }
        })
    )   
}

download_files(files_pulse)
```

## Download 7810 data files

```{r download-7810}
# Filter to necessary files
files_pulse <- drive_ls(
  path = GDRIVE_FOLDER,
  recursive = TRUE,
  pattern = "TG10.*data$")

message("Found ", nrow(files_pulse), " files")

download_files(files_pulse)

# 7810 files (full paths)
file.list.7810 <- list.files(path = RAW_DIR,
                             pattern = "TG10.*data$")

message("We have ", length(file.list.7810), " 7810 files")
```

## Split 7810 files into per-day files

```{r split-7810-files-prep}
ALREADY_SPLIT_LIST <- file.path(RAW_DIR, "LI7810_already_split_files.csv")

if(file.exists(ALREADY_SPLIT_LIST)) {
    already_split <- read_csv(ALREADY_SPLIT_LIST, col_types = "ccD")
} else {
    already_split <- tibble(file = character(0), hash = character(0), date = Date(0))    
}
```

This is a bit slow, as they're big files, so we keep track of 
what files have already been split in a simple CSV table `r ALREADY_SPLIT_LIST`.

```{r split-7810-files}
message("Splitting ", length(file.list.7810), " LI-7810 files")
for(f in file.list.7810) {
    # Check whether we've already split this file; name and hash both have to match
    dig <- digest::digest(file = file.path(RAW_DIR, f))
    if(nrow(filter(already_split, file == f, hash == dig)) == 1) {
        message(f, " has already been split; skipping")
        next
    }
    
    x <- ffi_read_LI7810(file.path(RAW_DIR, f))
    x$TIMESTAMP <- force_tz(x$TIMESTAMP, "EST")
    days <- format(x$TIMESTAMP, "%Y%m%d")
    for(d in unique(days)) {
        # Split files are "LI7810_YYYYMMDD.parquet"
        splitfile <- file.path(RAW_DIR, paste0("LI7810_", d, ".parquet"))
        if(file.exists(splitfile)) {
            message("\tAppending to ", splitfile)
            prevdata <- read_parquet(splitfile)
        } else {
            message("\tCreating ", splitfile)
            prevdata <- NULL
        }
        # Filter to this day, add any previous data, write out
        x[days == d,] |> 
            bind_rows(prevdata) |> 
            distinct() |> 
            arrange(TIMESTAMP) |> 
            write_parquet(splitfile)
        
    }
    # Record that we have split this file
    message("\tUpdating ", ALREADY_SPLIT_LIST)
    already_split |> 
        # remove any older entries for this file
        filter(!file == f) |> 
        # ...and add a new one
        bind_rows(tibble(file = f, hash = dig, date = Sys.Date())) ->
        already_split
    write_csv(already_split, file = ALREADY_SPLIT_LIST)
}
```

## Split 8100 files into observations and extract info

```{r split-8100-files-prep}
# Helper function: extract data from one observation in a LI-8100 file
# dat_raw is a vector of lines from the file
process_obs <- function(dat_raw, model) {
    # Make sure this is the desired model
    file_model <- substr(dat_raw[1], 1, 7)
    if(file_model != model) stop("This does not appear to be a ", model, " file!")
    
    # Save the observation number
    obs <- trimws(gsub("Obs#:\t", "", dat_raw[7], fixed = TRUE))
    # Save the observation length
    obs_length <- trimws(gsub("Observation Length:\t", "", dat_raw[10], fixed = TRUE))
    # Save the machine serial number
    sn <- trimws(gsub("Serial Number:\t", "", dat_raw[4], fixed = TRUE))
    # Parse the collar label from the header
    label <- trimws(gsub("Label:\t", "", dat_raw[9], fixed = TRUE))
    # Parse the collar number from the header
    chamber <- trimws(gsub("Chamber:\t", "", dat_raw[14], fixed = TRUE))
    # Parse the chamber volume from the header
    Vtotal <- trimws(gsub("Vtotal:\t", "", dat_raw[25], fixed = TRUE))
    # Parse the dead band from the footer
    DeadBand <- trimws(gsub("Dead Band:\t", "", dat_raw[length(dat_raw)-2], fixed = TRUE))
    # Parse the closing time from the header and use it to make a collar field
    TimeClosing <- trimws(gsub("TimeClosing:\t", "", dat_raw[length(dat_raw)-1], fixed = TRUE))
    
    # Log assembled data
    extracted <- tibble(SN = sn,
                        label = label,
                        chamber = chamber,
                        Vtotal = Vtotal,
                        obs_length = obs_length,
                        DeadBand = DeadBand,
                        TimeClosing = TimeClosing)
    
    # These files have 30 header lines, the column names in line 31,
    # and then the column units in line 7. We only want the names and then data
    total_lines = length(dat_raw)
    lines_to_skip <- 30
    lines_to_read <- total_lines - 30 - 25
    
    extracted$lines_read <- lines_to_read
    if(lines_to_read < 0) {
        negative_line_count <<- negative_line_count + 1
        return(extracted)
    }
    
    # We read directly from the string vector; much faster than writing
    # out and reading back in
    dat_read <- read.delim(textConnection(dat_raw),
        skip = lines_to_skip,
        nrows = lines_to_read,
        sep = "\t",
        header = TRUE)
    
    # Get first and last timestamp
    extracted$start_time <- first(dat_read$Date)
    extracted$end_time <- last(dat_read$Date)
    
    # Get average of environmental variables (V1-V4)
    warning_occurred <- tryCatch({
        extracted$Tcham <- mean(dat_read$Tcham, na.rm = TRUE)
        extracted$Pressure <- mean(dat_read$Pressure, na.rm = TRUE)
        extracted$V1_avg <- mean(dat_read$V1, na.rm = TRUE)
        extracted$V2_avg <- mean(dat_read$V2, na.rm = TRUE)
        extracted$V3_avg <- mean(dat_read$V3, na.rm = TRUE)
        extracted$V4_avg <- mean(dat_read$V4, na.rm = TRUE)
        FALSE
    }, warning = function(w) {
        warning_count <<- warning_count + 1
        TRUE
    })
    
    extracted$warning <-  warning_occurred
    
    return(extracted)
}


# List extracted 8100 files
file.list.8100 <- list.files(path = RAW_DIR, pattern = "81x$")
message("We have ", length(file.list.8100), " LI-8100 files")

# Look for an existing processed metadata file
if(file.exists(PROCESSED_FILE)) {
    message("Reading existing ", PROCESSED_FILE)
    processed <- read_parquet(PROCESSED_FILE)    
    message("(remove this file to re-run everything from scratch)")
} else {
    message("Creating new ", PROCESSED_FILE)
    processed <- tibble()
}
```


```{r split-8100-files}

# Go through the split files, read and process, add to processed table
# Write out table every so often so we don't lose our progress
skip_obs_count <- 0
processed_obs_count <- 0
negative_line_count <- 0
warning_count <- 0

for (i in seq_along(file.list.8100)) {
    f <- file.list.8100[i]
    message(i, "/", length(file.list.8100), " Reading ", f, "... ")
    lines <- readLines(file.path(RAW_DIR, f))
    f_no_extension <- gsub(".81x$", "", f)
    
    # Find all the lines that start with LI-8100 in this file
    l8100 <- grep("^LI-8100", lines)
    n_obs <- length(l8100)
    # Add one at end so that 'last' calculation below works for final entry
    l8100 <- c(l8100, length(lines) + 1) 
    
    # How many result rows are already in the processed table? If identical
    # to numbers of observations to process, assume we already have this file
    # and move on
    if(nrow(processed) > 0) {
        n_processed <- length(grep(f_no_extension, processed$obs, fixed = TRUE))
        if(n_processed == n_obs) {
            message("\t", n_processed, " observations already processed; moving on") 
            next
        } else {
            # remove any old data for this file (in case it was previously
            # partially processed, for example)
            processed <- filter(processed, !grepl(f_no_extension, obs, fixed = TRUE))
        }
    }
    
    # Process each observation, saving results in a list
    file_results <- list()
    for(i in seq_along(head(l8100, -1))) {
        first <- l8100[i]
        last <- l8100[i+1] - 1
        file_results[[i]] <- process_obs(lines[first:last], model = "LI-8100")
        file_results[[i]]$obs <- i
    }
    processed_obs_count <- processed_obs_count + n_obs
    file_dat <- bind_rows(file_results) |> mutate(file = f_no_extension)
    
    # Add to processed data and write out
    processed |> 
        bind_rows(file_dat) -> 
        processed
    write_parquet(processed, PROCESSED_FILE)
    message("\tProcessed ", n_obs, " observations")
} # for i
```

## Join with collar metadata

```{r collar-map}
message("Reading collar map...")
collar_metadata <- read_csv(file.path("metadata", "collar_map.csv"),
                            col_types = "ccic_")

processed %>% 
    left_join(collar_metadata, 
              by = c("label" = "Collar"),
              relationship = "many-to-one") ->
    processed_collars
```

```{r diagnostics}
message("How many files generated a warning?")
processed_collars |> 
    group_by(warning) |> 
    summarise(n = n()) |> 
    mutate(percent = round(n / sum(n) * 100, 2))

ggplot(processed_collars, aes(lines_read)) +
    geom_histogram(bins = 30)
```
